sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Opening with the heading and date of the maamar.

translations.translation: With the help of Heaven.
19 Kislev 5739*

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Explains that the dispersion of Israel among the nations is a divine charity, enabling Jews in free lands to strengthen those under persecution to observe Torah and mitzvos.

translations.translation: Rabbi Oshaya said: What is the meaning of that which is written,
“The righteousness of His strong ones in Israel… The Holy One, blessed be He, performed an act of charity with Israel by scattering them among the nations,”
And it is explained by the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the leader, in his maamar beginning with the words “Zeh”
[which was said on 19 Kislev
of the year 5689 at the festive meal,
and was printed in the pamphlet “Drushei Chasunah” of 5689],
that through the fact that Israel are scattered in many countries,
behold, even when in one country they oppress and pressure the Children of Israel and do not allow them to study Torah and fulfill mitzvos,
to the extent that regarding several mitzvos they are literally compelled [against their will]
that they have no possibility at all to fulfill them even through self-sacrifice,
[For example,
when there is a royal decree not to bring the Four Species into the country,
then even through self-sacrifice it is impossible to fulfill the mitzvah],
behold, through the fact that the Jews who are in the other countries engage in Torah and mitzvos,
they give strength and might also to those who are in the place where there are decrees,
so that they will be able to study Torah and fulfill mitzvos.
And from the light to the heavy,
first that they will be able to fulfill the mitzvos through self-sacrifice at least
[as is known that there is an opinion among the halachic authorities
that even regarding mitzvos about which they said “transgress and do not be killed,” one is permitted to sanctify the Name and give himself over],
and until afterwards they will not need self-sacrifice at all,
and until they will have no trials and not even hindrances and delays,
for they will go out to freedom and will be able to engage in Torah and mitzvos out of expansiveness,
as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said,
“Whoever fulfills the Torah out of poverty, will ultimately fulfill it out of wealth.”

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Explains that this charity applies spiritually everywhere, as one Jew can redeem another from captivity to the evil inclination in areas where he himself is not enslaved.

translations.translation: B)
Now, since the Torah is eternal in every time and season and in every place
(as explained in the maamar),
it is understood that this charity also applies in places where there are no decrees against Torah and mitzvos.
And this will be understood based on what the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the leader, said
(in the aforementioned Drushei Chasunah)
regarding the matter of the mitzvah of redeeming captives, which also exists in spirituality.
For just as a captive in the physical sense
(one who sits in prison)
cannot leave from there,
so too is it in spirituality,
that sometimes a person is captive, heaven forfend, in the hands of his evil inclination
[and this is like businessmen who are extremely busy and troubled by the troubles of their business,
who are bound
(captive)
in confusing thoughts and cannot get out of them],
and to the point that sometimes he is like one who is compelled,
and in the language of the Rambam
(regarding halachah)
“his evil inclination overpowered him.”
And this is the matter of the charity through His scattering them among the nations, also regarding places of ease,
for when a Jew is captive in the hands of his evil inclination, heaven forfend,
(regarding a particular matter),
his release from captivity is
[not through his own power,
since “a prisoner cannot free himself from his imprisonment,”
but rather]
through a Jew who is not in captivity regarding this matter.
That is to say,
that even when the one who redeems him from captivity is himself captive in the hands of his evil inclination,
and to the point that he is like one who is compelled
(his evil inclination overpowered him)
regarding another mitzvah,
nevertheless,
since regarding many mitzvos he is not captive in the hands of his evil inclination,
for the opposition of the evil inclination for each person is
(primarily)
in a different matter
[for just as
in every time there is a particular service most relevant to that time,
and the main temptations and opposition of the evil inclination are to prevent this service,
therefore the trials of one generation differ from the trials of other generations
[like in the time of Menasheh when the inclination for idolatry was dominant,
unlike in the generations after him,
all the more so after they killed the inclination for idolatry],
so too is it within one time itself,
that each Jew has a particular matter
(a mitzvah or custom and the like)
that is most relevant to him,
as is known
in the explanation of our Rabbis, of blessed memory, saying,
“Your father, in what was he most careful?”
and the main temptations and opposition of his evil inclination are regarding this matter],
And through his fulfilling the mitzvos against which his evil inclination does not fight
(so much),
he redeems from captivity the one whose evil inclination overpowered him regarding these mitzvos.
And this is “The Holy One, blessed be He, performed an act of charity with Israel by scattering them among the nations,”
for redeeming captives is the most elevated charity,
and as explained in the aforementioned maamar
that regarding the mitzvah of charity, redeeming captives takes precedence over everything, and there is no mitzvah as great as redeeming captives,
And through His scattering them among the nations,
so that the evil inclination of one differs from the evil inclination of the other,
through this the charity of redeeming captives is fulfilled,
as above.
